statement.p: Let \vec{v}_1=\left[\begin{array}{c} 0\cr 1\cr 2 \end{array}\right], \vec{v}_2 = \left[\begin{array}{c} 1\cr -1\cr 0 \end{array}\right], \vec{v}_3 = \left[\begin{array}{c} 1\cr 0\cr -1 \end{array}\right] be eigenvectors of the matrix A which correspond to the eigenvalues \lambda_1 = -2, \lambda_2 = -1, and \lambda_3 = 1, respectively, and let \vec{x}=\left[\begin{array}{c} 4\cr -1\cr 0 \end{array}\right].
Express \vec{x} as a linear combination of \vec{v}_1, \vec{v}_2, and \vec{v}_3, and find A\vec{x}.
